---
name: workflow-discovery
description: Clarify an ambiguous workflow request before designing or changing its graph.
---

# Workflow Discovery

When the request is incomplete or uses ambiguous terms, conduct a Socratic interview before editing the workflow. Ask at most six questions, one at a time, and choose each next question from the previous answer. Before each question, state in one sentence what the answer changed in your understanding. Separate facts, interpretations, value judgments, and desired outcomes. Test ambiguous keywords, hidden assumptions, evidence, competing explanations, and what each conclusion would imply. Ask only questions that could change the workflow design or its acceptance criteria.

Stop as soon as the requirements are sufficient. Then summarize: the initial question, the underlying problem, confirmed facts, unverified assumptions, variables most likely to change the design, and one precise actionable question. Wait for the user to confirm that question before committing a graph or running side effects. Do not ask for a workflow name, ID, JSON, or manual node configuration; derive those after confirmation.
